title: Zonin
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Avodah Zarah 55a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.55a.4), Zonin tells Rabbi Akiva, “You and I both know that idolatry has no substance, yet we see people who go there broken and return healed.” [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Avodah_Zarah.55a.4.1) explains that Zonin was Jewish, but Hyman thinks the wording suggests he was a gentile, an inference also argued by Maharsha in [Chiddushei Aggadot](https://www.sefaria.org/Chidushei_Agadot_on_Avodah_Zarah.55a.2).[^1]

notes.text: Rashi says outright that Zonin was Jewish. Maharsha says he would accept that as a received tradition, but reads Zonin’s wording as suggesting that he outwardly practiced idolatry and privately doubted it. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1109&lang=en) records both approaches.
